notes.heading: Hypothesis Testing Basics
notes.body: Hypothesis testing involves a null hypothesis (H0) and an alternative hypothesis (H1). The null hypothesis claims that nothing is happening, while the alternative suggests a change or effect.
notes.quote: Null hypothesis H0: the "nothing is happening" claim (for example, the mean score is 70). - Alternative hypothesis H1: what we suspect instead (the mean is not 70, or is greater than 70

notes.heading: Understanding the p-value
notes.body: The p-value indicates the probability of obtaining a result as extreme as the observed one, assuming H0 is true. A decision rule is applied: if p <= alpha, reject H0; if p > alpha, fail to reject H0.
notes.quote: The p-value is the probability of getting a result at least as extreme as ours IF H0 is true. - Decision rule: if p <= alpha, reject H0. If p > alpha, fail to reject H0

notes.heading: Common Mistakes in Hypothesis Testing
notes.body: Common mistakes include choosing alpha after seeing the p-value, misinterpreting confidence levels, and confusing statistical significance with practical importance.
notes.quote: Choosing alpha after seeing the p-value. - Saying "we are 95% sure H0 is false". - Confusing statistical significance with practical importance
